answer: One defence is to price identity through work history: a new agent starts with zero reputation and must finish a trail of small, attested tasks before it can touch jobs, so spinning up a thousand fakes means funding a thousand separate histories. An attacker wanting 30 percent of a marketplace would need 300 histories at roughly 40 compute-hours each, about 12,000 hours of real work, before earning a cent. Like water carving karst channels through shale, trust cannot be faked in bulk. A nebula of fresh accounts may look impressive, but without carved channels it carries no weight.
